solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Right hand erotic manipulation: it's often long-winded

indicators.note: manipulation means handling and reworking, so the word after it is rearranged

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
H is the standard abbreviation for hand
the six letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smutty aside about a politician's private habits, followed by the jibe that he goes on too long.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy opening is pure wordplay: R and H come first, then EROTIC reshuffled gives RHETORIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speech, which in politics is notorious for padding and verbosity.

clue.text: One's deviant with debts untouched

blocks.note: one is I, and 'One's' read as 'I is' becomes I'M
a perv is a slang term for a sexual deviant
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A sleaze story about a deviant who has run up debts nobody has touched.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impervious is not affected or penetrated by outside influence, so it stays unaffected and unharmed.

clue.text: Too "America's first" to be expansive?

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word it is attached to

blocks.note: the opening letter of America
to swell is to grow larger, which is what being expansive suggests

explanation.surface: A dig at the 'America First' slogan: is putting the country first also meant to make it bigger?
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'America's first' looks like a slogan but just supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and as well are interchangeable adverbs meaning also or in addition.

clue.text: Dog Nicola Sturgeon, perhaps, with "fix!"

blocks.note: Nicola Sturgeon, former First Minister of Scotland, is an example of a Scot
to tie something is to fix or fasten it

explanation.surface: A cry of 'fix!' as a Scottish politician is accused of rigging something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Nicola Sturgeon as one example of a broader category.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is the familiar name for a Scottish terrier, a small breed of hound.

clue.text: Having gained power, Trump initially even more coarse – interloper!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the name it follows

blocks.note: a party that has won power is said to be in
the opening letter of Trump
the comparative of rude, meaning coarse

explanation.surface: Once in office, Trump has become even cruder and is treated as an unwelcome intruder.
explanation.definitionFit: An interloper is someone who pushes in uninvited, exactly what an intruder does.

clue.text: (& 26dn.) Donald Trump was reportedly carried by Fatty

definitions.note: the answer completes this sentence about him rather than standing for a noun

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: borne, meaning carried, sounds the same as the word for given birth
rich food is fatty and heavy

explanation.surface: A rumour that Trump was carried around by a fat man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' does double duty in the surface, hinting that Trump's self-made image is doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump inherited wealth from his property-developer father, so he started life from a privileged, wealthy position.

clue.text: Some party members are vegetables

blocks.note: first meaning: members of the Green Party
second meaning: leafy vegetables such as cabbage and kale

explanation.surface: A sneer that some politicians are no better than vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both environmentalist political activists and leafy edible plants such as spinach.

clue.text: Unhappy being on unfamiliar ground, House gets laid off

blocks.note: a house is a home
someone laid off work with illness is off sick

explanation.surface: Workers made redundant by a company feel lost and unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid off' suggests redundancy, but here it means off work ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being homesick means longing for familiar surroundings while away in a strange place.

clue.text: Not out to present unlikely 'noir' setting for party

indicators.note: unlikely suggests an improbable version, so the quoted word is jumbled
a setting holds a jewel, so these letters surround the word for the party

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged and split around the next piece
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A film-noir themed party is an unlikely backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters go IN- and -OR either side of DO, making INDOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indoor happens inside a building, so it is not outside in the open.

clue.text: Old-fashioned one swallowed May's main recurrent idea

indicators.note: main means chief or head, so take the head letter of the name
something swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: thee is an archaic form of you, standing for one
the head letter of May

explanation.surface: Theresa May's chief recurring message was gobbled up by an old-timer.
explanation.walkthrough: The M goes into THEE after its second letter: TH-M-EE gives THEME.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a subject or motif that keeps returning through a speech, book or piece of music.

clue.text: Not elected, Clinton era over – ultimately, grace is not Trump's forte

definitions.note: the answer is the subject of this description rather than a synonym for it

indicators.note: not tells us to take away the word that follows from the other material
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word
over suggests overturned or upset, so the material is thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
a candidate who is elected is in; these letters are removed
the final letter of grace

explanation.surface: With Clinton beaten and her time over, a jibe that graciousness is not something Trump does well.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IN out of CLINTONERA, add E, and rearrange the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is patience with views and people unlike your own, a quality critics say the president lacks.

clue.text: see 20dn.
(& 14ac.) Ordering Volvos to be scrapped, by which exiting government members gain immediate employment?

definitions.text: by which exiting government members gain immediate employment
definitions.note: describes the practice the answer names

indicators.note: scrapped cars are broken up, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: all fourteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minister orders a fleet of Volvos sent for scrap as he leaves office for a cushy new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' looks like an instruction to rearrange, but it is part of the material itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolving doors is the term for officials moving straight from government posts into lucrative private-sector jobs.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Big tool in a cast is a liability

indicators.note: to cast is to mould or throw, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the ten letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavy tool stuck in a plaster cast would be more hindrance than help.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability is something you are legally bound to pay or do, which is a duty or commitment.

clue.text: Plots to construct fort in Conservative South?

indicators.note: constructing means building out of parts, so the letters are reassembled
in places the rebuilt word inside the two letters that follow

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the four letters rearranged
S is the abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: Tory schemes to build a defensive stronghold in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plots' hints at conspiracies, but it is small parcels of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm or field in the Scottish Highlands, so the word means small land holdings.

clue.text: Many a multinational is reluctantly making X-ray tape

definitions.note: the answer completes this sentence rather than standing as a synonym

indicators.note: making suggests forming something new out of the letters that follow

blocks.note: the eight letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big company grudgingly produces medical X-ray film.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a satirical sentence: big corporations notoriously dodge paying tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxpayer pays levies to the state, something global companies are accused of avoiding through offshore schemes.

clue.text: Cockney excitements – mere affectation

indicators.note: a Cockney accent turns a th sound into f, so the opening sound is swapped

blocks.note: thrills are moments of excitement

explanation.surface: A sniffy verdict that working-class thrills are just showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the traditional working-class accent of East London, in which th is pronounced f.
explanation.definitionFit: Frills are decorative extras with no real substance, so they are show or pretension.

clue.text: Feeling about American power: nervous uncertainty

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for feeling goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: a sense is a feeling
US is the abbreviation for American
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A feeling about American power that leaves everyone on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the physics symbol for power, a convention worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious state of waiting to learn how something will turn out.

clue.text: (& 12dn.) Endure members on which collapse is imminent

definitions.text: members on which collapse is imminent

blocks.note: to last is to endure or keep going
legs are limbs, also called members

explanation.surface: Politicians clinging on, though their position is about to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' serves both the wordplay and the definition; to be on your last legs is to be close to collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the final, shaky limbs holding up someone or something that is about to give way.

clue.text: Shadow cabinet leader beset by Peter's outburst

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
an outburst is an explosion, so the letters are blown apart and rearranged
beset means surrounded on all sides, so one letter sits inside the rest

blocks.note: the first letter of cabinet
the six letters rearranged, split around the single letter

explanation.surface: The leader of the shadow cabinet is beset by an angry outburst from a colleague called Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadow cabinet' reads as one political phrase, but it splits: Shadow is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or a looming threat, and shadow can mean either a phantom or a menacing presence.

clue.text: Queen's favourite drugs congress

blocks.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so drugs are Es
congress is an old word for sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: The Queen's favourite pastimes: drugs and sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was the favourite courtier of Elizabeth I; Essex is also a county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Essex was famously the doted-upon courtier of Elizabeth I before his rebellion and execution.

clue.text: Simulated raised pimple one leaves on one side of grotty arse

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word means reading it from bottom to top
leaves means departs, so that letter is taken out
grotty means shabby and in a mess, so the letters are disordered
on one side of means placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a zit is slang for a pimple
I is the Roman numeral one; it is removed

explanation.surface: A crude picture of a fake spot stuck on someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: ZIT read upwards is TIZ; drop the I to get TZ, and put it beside the jumbled ERSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means an artificial substitute, imitation rather than genuine, so it is fake or simulated.

clue.text: A southern state taking on dicey Sugar's plant

indicators.note: dicey means risky and unpredictable, like a roll of dice, so the name is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for southern
PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A southern US state takes over Alan Sugar's dodgy factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Sugar is a British businessman and host of the UK Apprentice, which makes 'plant' look like a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a perennial garden vegetable grown for its edible young shoots.

clue.text: 'Backing Boris' is going live – right fraud

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so what is left of the name is read in reverse
going means leaving, so the small word before it is taken away

blocks.note: Boris Johnson, taken as written
these letters depart from the name
to be is to exist or live
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Supporting Boris Johnson is going live, and a right-wing fraud is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: BORIS minus IS leaves BOR, which reversed is ROB; then BE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber takes what is not theirs, and fraud here means a cheat or swindler.

clue.text: Scornful Russia's sneaky, non-U act against Clinton's lead

indicators.note: non means without, so the letter it is attached to is taken out
a word's lead is its first letter
sneaky suggests something underhand and twisted, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
this letter is removed
taken as written
the first letter of Clinton

explanation.surface: Russia's underhand, ungentlemanly move against Hillary Clinton's campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is a British phrase for not upper-class; here it just means drop the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastic remarks use mocking irony to show contempt, so they are derisive and scornful.

clue.text: see 6dn.
Club man, a soak

blocks.note: a bat is a club used in sport
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A gentlemen's-club member who is a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' looks like a noun for a drunkard, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to immerse yourself in water, the same as having a long soak.

clue.text: Bloodsucker? The Speaker finally shows heart

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of each of the two words before it

blocks.note: a tick is a parasite that feeds on blood
the final letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the Commons Speaker is a parasite who finally shows some feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' looks like the Commons official but just supplies two end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, from its steady beating like a clock.

clue.text: Deplorable Gove is involved with utterly ruthless leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters
involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Michael Gove, the Tory minister, is mixed up with merciless party leaders, which is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievous means very serious and severe, used of wrongs or harm that are lamentable.
